images.note: Primary: half-plate ambrotype by William Judkins Thomson, Monmouth, Illinois, October 11, 1858 -- taken mid-campaign, two days before the Quincy debate; fully contemporary. Alt: albumen print by William Marsh, Springfield, May 20, 1860 (two days after the Republican presidential nomination); contemporary but post-debates, same beardless appearance. | Alt removed: Met DP274831 collides with u5l8-lincoln-1860 primary.
images.title: Abraham Lincoln, October 1858 (ambrotype)

images.note: Primary: salted paper print by McClees & Vannerson, c. 1859; contemporary. Alt: 'Senator Stephen A. Douglas of Illinois,' 1861 (World Digital Library via LOC); contemporary portrait, post-debates (Douglas died June 1861).
images.title: Stephen A. Douglas, c. 1859 (photograph)

images.note: Primary: daguerreotype, ca. 1855, artist unknown; contemporary. Alt: quarter-plate ambrotype, c. 1856, unidentified artist, CC0; contemporary. Serves the Foner-paraphrase beat naming Douglass as the principled-egalitarian contrast. | Primary swapped: Met DT1144 collides with u5l8-douglass primary; promoted the NPG c.1856 ambrotype (CC0) to primary.
images.title: Frederick Douglass, c. 1855-56 (daguerreotype/ambrotype)

images.note: Title page of 'Political Debates Between Hon. Abraham Lincoln and Hon. Stephen A. Douglas,' Follett, Foster & Co., Columbus, 1860 -- the campaign book the script describes ('printed as a book and used as a campaign document'). Two different physical copies/scans; both served via Internet Archive (curl -L: page URLs 302 to the BookReader image server).
images.source: Internet Archive (Lincoln Financial Foundation Collection copy)
images.title: 'Political Debates' title page, 1860 first edition

images.note: Page 1 of Lincoln's Springfield speech as printed in the 1860 book, showing the 'A house divided against itself cannot stand' passage -- a primary-document visual for the quoted speech. The book heads it 'June 17, 1858'; the speech was delivered June 16 (book's dating error, preserved honestly).
images.source: Internet Archive (Lincoln Financial Foundation Collection copy)
images.title: House Divided speech text, as printed 1860

images.note: Table of Contents of the 1860 book listing all seven joint debates with towns and dates (Ottawa Aug 21 through Alton Oct 15, 1858) -- directly visualizes the 'seven Illinois towns' beat.
images.source: Internet Archive (Lincoln Financial Foundation Collection copy)
images.title: Table of Contents listing the seven debates, 1860

images.note: Primary: 'Indiana, Illinois, Missouri & Iowa with parts of adjoining states,' 1858 -- exactly contemporary railroad map; all seven debate towns were rail towns. Alt: 'New sectional map of the state of Illinois,' 1852 (BPL) -- more detailed but six years pre-debates; all seven towns established and shown.
images.title: Illinois railroad map, 1858

images.note: Primary: J.H. Colton 'Nebraska and Kansas,' 1855 -- the two territories the 1854 act organized; shows what 'let the territories vote' meant geographically. Alt: 'A new map of Nebraska, Kansas, New Mexico, and Indian Territories,' 1856 (BPL).
images.title: Nebraska and Kansas territories map, 1855

images.note: Broadside advertising the Lincoln-Douglas debate at Freeport on August 27 (Ralph E. Becker Collection of Political Americana, NMAH; SI 'associated date' 1858-08-27). CAUTION: typographic style suggests a 20th-century reproduction rather than an 1858 original -- treat as later commemorative, not a verified contemporary broadside. No second institution verified at the bar; alt null.
images.source: Smithsonian Institution, National Museum of American History
images.title: Freeport debate broadside (August 27)

images.note: Carte-de-visite portrait of Lincoln, 1860 (World Digital Library via LOC); the standing pose with hand on books is Mathew Brady's celebrated February 27, 1860 sitting -- the day Lincoln spoke at Cooper Union. WDL record dates it 1860 without naming the studio; Brady attribution follows the standard O-55 identification. A second Brady 1860 from another institution could not be verified at the size bar (NPG holds Brady Lincolns but SI rate-limited verification; the Met has none); alt null.
images.title: Lincoln carte-de-visite, 1860 (Brady)
